source_notes: README: q:"a robust and flexible framework for Bayesian Optimization"; 2.x has multi-fidelity, multi-thread, ask-and-tell; since 2.4.0 default surrogate is scikit-learn RF. No benchmark numbers on the page (benchmark folder not opened). OOD split idea: tune on instance families A, hidden test on unseen family B (e.g. different structure/size). Levers: search-space definition, conditional params, instance-feature selection, racing/cutoff scheduling, ensembling configs (portfolio). INFERRED: depends on target; with cutoff 10 s x 100 hidden instances /8 cores about 2-3 min per final eval, hours for tuning loop. Single-source.
source_version: Baseline: target solver at its default parameter configuration on the training instances; agent may also write its own tuner. -> Reference: SMAC3 (random-forest surrogate + racing) run for a fixed wall budget on the same training instances, best incumbent evaluated on hidden instances.

facts.claim: SMAC3 repository exists at github.com/automl/SMAC3, described as a Bayesian optimization / hyperparameter optimization package
SMAC3 licence is 3-clause BSD, stated in LICENSE.txt (the SPDX field NOASSERTION is a detection gap, not a licence problem)
SMAC3 release v2.4.1 exists; its notes list three bugfixes (sklearn DTYPE alias removal, forbidden clauses preservation, pytest-cases removal) and do not describe a solver portfolio or selector
Since SMAC3 2.4.0 the default surrogate is a scikit-learn random forest
The seed's three open local-search solvers for one problem class are named and their licences are known
A public algorithm selection benchmark format with runtimes and instance features exists (ASlib), so the selection recipe is documented and the task overlaps a known subject
Per-instance runtime-regression selectors for SAT (SATzilla) are published methods, so the reference recipe is recallable

The smoke build was not run because there is no named artifact to build.

spike_plan.kill_if: Solvers cannot be named or built offline, or the held-out family shows no gap between selector and single-best solver.
spike_plan.pass_if: Named open solvers build offline; VBS PAR10 is clearly below single-best PAR10 on training families; a simple RF selector beats single-best on the held-out family by a measurable margin; results are deterministic across three reruns.
steps: Name the three local-search solvers and confirm each has an open licence and a build. Stop here if none can be named.
Obtain or generate training runtimes (PAR10 under a cutoff) and instance features for at least two instance families; check that the single best solver and virtual best solver differ.
Fit a random-forest runtime regressor per solver with scikit-learn and select argmin predicted runtime; score PAR10 on a held-out family.
Repeat with the family held out to measure the OOD gap against the single best solver.
Check determinism: rerun the selector three times with fixed seeds and compare PAR10.
Confirm the single-process CPU-time accounting blocks parallel solver runs before any scoring.

v1.summary: The seed cites SMAC3 v2.4.1 (BSD-3, confirmed) as the source for a per-instance selector over three unnamed local-search solvers, but SMAC3 is a Bayesian optimization package with no selector or portfolio, and the solvers, data and reference are not identified. Killed under K2 because the subject has no real artifact to ground the bundle; a re-seed would need named solvers with an open licence and a public runtime dataset, such as an ASlib-format scenario.
